sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB / NH-7 /
CR / 68/2011-12 dated 30.11.2021 pertaining to Sy. No.9/1 measuring 130 Sq. meters of Hunasamaranahalli village, Jala Hobli, Bengaluru North (Addl) Taluka, Bengaluru Urban District.

.2. The definite case of the petitioner is that the property of respondent No.1 measuring 130 Sq.
meters in Sy. No.9/1 of Hunasamaranahalli village has been acquired under Preliminary Notification issued by the respondent No.2 under Section 3A(1) vide S.O. No.3159 (E) dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification under A.P. No.162/2022 Section 3D(1) and (2) vide S.O. No.
1622(E) dated 02.07.2010 and passed the award on 22.03.2011 and awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.9,36,953/-, which has been received by the respondent No.1 under protest.
Subsequently, on 08.02.2012 the respondent No.1 has filed the application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.6,000/- per Sq. feet.
Accordingly, the application is taken by the respondent No.2 for consideration.

.3. Thereafter, the Arbitrator hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ / ARB / NH-7/ CR 97(A)89/88/68/2011-12 dated 30.11.2021.
.4.
Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting aside the following:

:GROUNDS:
The petitioner claims that the impugned is liable to be set aside since it is bad in law,
in conflict with public policy of A.P. No.162/2022 India and patently illegal.
The award has been rendered mechanically without adverting to the relevant provisions of law.
The Arbitrator failed to considered the market value of the acquired land as on the date of notification under Section 3A of the Act.
The respondent No.1 has not filed or produced any documents or records to substantiate his claim for enhancement as made in the proceedings impugned.
The impugned Arbitral Award is against the well settled law of fixation of compensation and the public Exchequer should not be put to undue burden by excess valuation.

Further, no findings are given by the Arbitrator in exercise of his jurisdiction under Section 3G(5) of the NH Act in determining the market value based on the use/category of the land as on the date of acquisition,
which alone can be taken into account.

That the cause of action for this petition arose on 30.11.2021, when the Arbitral Award was passed within the jurisdiction of A.P.
No.162/2022 this Court.
The petition is filed within the period of limitation as extended by the Hon'ble Supreme Court and among other grounds, prayed for relief claimed in the petition.

sentences.text: The petitioner along with the petition filed I.A. No.1 under Section 34(3) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 to condone the delay of 29 days in filing the petition.

.6. The above application is supported with the affidavit of petitioner, wherein, it is stated that the petitioner received copy of the award dated 30.11.2021 with a direction to pay the enhanced amount to the respondent No.1 in claim No.LAQ / ARB / NH-07 / CR / 68 / 2011-12.
Further, during pandemic there was a change in the post for Project Director and the post remained vacant for several months and he has succeeded the post of Project Director of the applicant.

Further in the month of February and March 2022, several employees of the applicant tested positive for A.P.
No.162/2022 Covid-19 and the office was completely non-functional.

Due to the aforesaid reasons,
the concerned department of their office could not co-ordinate with their legal counsel to pass instructions and further to furnish relevant records to challenge the order passed by respondent No.2.
Hence, there is a delay of 29 days in filing the above petition is bonafide reason but not intentional.
Among other grounds prayed for condonation of delay if any in filing the petition.
.7. The respondent No.1 has not filed any objections to the IA.
.8. The respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel.
The respondent No.2 though served with the notice, not chosen to appear before this Court to resist the petition and hence, the respondent No.2 has been placed exparte.

The entire records in LAQ / ARB / NH- 7/ CR 97(A)89/88/68/2011-12 dated 30.11.2021.
.9.

On the basis of above, the points for consideration are as under:
A.P. No.162/2022 1) Whether the petition filed by the petitioner is within time?
2) Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?
3) What order or award?
.10.
Heard the arguments.

Perused the materials on record, on that basis my findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 & 2 : In the Affirmative Point No.3 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS .11. POINT No. 1: Perused the I.A. No.1 along with affidavit that has been filed for condonation of delay in filing the petition, satisfied with reasons therein and the said application is not opposed by the respondent No. 1.
Accordingly, I am of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to condone the delay in filing the petition.

sentences.text: Accordingly the point No. 1 is answered in the affirmative.
.12. Point No.2:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note the admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The respondent No.1 G. Anand is an owner of the property bearing Sy. No.9/1 measuring to an extent of 130 Square Meters of Hunasamaranahalli village and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-7 under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 02.07.2010
, is an admitted fact.

It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the respondent No.2 has enhanced the compensation from Rs.7,413/- per Sq. meters to Rs.
14,827/- per Sq. meter.
It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.9,36,953/- was disbursed to the respondent No. 1 as compensation.

.13. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the respondent No. 1 G.
Anand filed an application before the respondent No.2 claiming that he is entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs.
A.P. No.162/2022 6,000/- per Sq. feet as on 08.12.2012.
On the basis of said application, the respondent No. 2 hold an inquiry and passed an order in LAQ / ARB / NH-7 / CR / 68 / 2011-12 dated 30.11.2021.

The respondent No. 2 in its order enhanced the compensation at Rs.14,827/- per Sq. meter by adding Rs.7,620/- to the compensation decided by the respondent No. 3 i.e.,
Rs.7,207/- per Sq. meter.
.14.
The said enhancement of compensation has been challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No. 2 without considering the relevant provisions of NHA Act and also without considering the guidance value or market value of the property as on the date of Preliminary Notification, enhanced the compensation by relying on the guidance value of the year 2011-12 published vide notification bearing No. CVC/19/2010- 11 dated 21.09.2011 and the said document is not part of arbitration proceedings as well as subsequent to the preliminary notification dated 09.12.2009.

The A.P. No.162/2022 petitioner during the course of argument claimed that the decision of the respondent No.1 based on the said notification is without knowledge of the petitioner and said guidance value of the year 2011-12 has not been brought to the notice of the petitioner.
Accordingly, claimed that such award is liable to be set aside as per Section 24 of National Highways Authority Act.

In this context, the petitioner relied on the decision reported in (2019) 15 SCC 131 in a case of Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs.
National Highways Authority of India.

sentences.text: It is true that in the said decision, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that whatever the document relied by the Arbitrator shall be brought to the notice of the parties, so that the parties can make submission or give the rebuttal evidence about such documents.
Hence, it is necessary to see whether such notification is found in the records received by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2.
On perusal of entire records of the arbitration proceedings, it is nowhere discloses about obtaining of notification by the A.P. No.162/2022 respondent No. 2 before proceeding to pass the award.
Further, who has produced the said notification dated 21.09.2011 regarding guidance value of the year 2011- 12, is also not forth-coming.

In-fact, there is no material National Highways Authority Of India ... vs Anand G on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5484125/
4 on record to show that such notification is there bearing No. CVC/19/2010-11 dated 21.09.2011 issued by the Stamp and Registration Department.

sentences.text: In the entire order, nowhere discloses that the Arbitrator has brought the said notification to the knowledge of the petitioner.
In-fact, no document is found, which substantiate the enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Arbitrator.

.15. In the case on hand, though the respondent No.2 served with the notice not chosen to appear before the Court to resist the case of the petitioner or to support the award passed by the Arbitrator.
Absolutely there is no material placed before the Court to disbelieve the petitioner case or to substantiate the award passed by the Arbitrator.

Apart from that it is stated in the operative portion of the order that the respondent No. 2 A.P. No.162/2022 has increased 50% by using his discretion but how the said discretion has been used or what is the basis for using the said discretion is nowhere explained in the order.

The arbitrator is expected to give some reasons for the enhancement of 50% or under what circumstances, the respondent No.1 is entitle for said 50%
enhancement to be explained or reasoned by the Arbitrator, otherwise such discretion cannot be accepted as discretion has to be used or exercised judiciously.
Hence, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to intervene with the award passed by the Arbitrator and the award is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, the point No.2 is held in the affirmative.
.16. Point No.3:
In view of my above finding, I proceed to pass the following.
ORDER IA filed by the petitioner to condone the delay in filing the petition is allowed.
A.P. No.162/2022 Petition filed under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is hereby allowed.

Consequently, the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 in case No. LAQ / ARB / NH-7 / CR / 68/ 2011-12 dated 30.11.2021 pertaining to Sy. No.9/1 measuring 130 Sq. Meters of Hunasamaranahalli village is hereby set aside with a liberty to the parties to pursue their remedy in accordance with law.
